pulls.author: shipilev
pulls.body_excerpt: I noticed in workloads that have explicit GCs and low (or unset) Xms that we uncommit very aggressively, which eats performance. This change does much lazier commits, with deliberate waits between region uncommits. This allows application to swoop in more promptly and claim empty regions for allocations, which saves a trip through uncommit->commit sequence. Since uncommit is now running for longer, it is now profitable to figure out the uncommit plan right away, sort regions by target uncommit time and (slowly) work through them. So glyph width and rowBytes are not same, and when we convert this LCD Glyph into BGRA data in MTLTextRenderer.m we are not considering this padding and it corrupts the text.
